newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Clabecq wins stay of execution.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Clabecq wins stay of execution.

text.p: A Belgian commercial court has ruled against declaring Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq bankrupt and has instead appointed two experts to assess the company's situation, a court spokesman said on Friday.

"Clabecq is not bankrupt...two experts have been appointed and they have to submit a first report to the court by Tuesday, December 24," the court official in the southern town of Nivelles told Reuters. He gave no further details.
Clabecq filed for bankruptcy on Thursday after its majority shareholder, Belgium's southern Walloon region, decided to withdraw its support.

The fate of the loss-making steel firm, which employs about 1,700 people, appeared to have been sealed on Wednesday when the European Commission rejected a rescue plan by the Walloon region for Clabecq.

The project involved an offer of 1.5 billion Belgian francs of capital, 700 million francs of credit - which had already granted, the writing-off of debts worth more than 800 million francs and the rescheduling of other borrowings.
The Commission said the subsidies went against EU rules which only allow steel sector aid for environmental reasons, for research and development or for company closure.
Walloon government Minister-President Robert Collignon was quoted on Thursday as saying the government reserved the right to appeal against the Commission's decision to reject its rescue plan.
Collignon hopes that a certain amount of activity could be preserved at Clabecq, notably the blast furnace to supply near-by privately-owned small steel firm Usines Gustave Boel.
The Brussels bourse announced later on Friday that Clabecq would remain suspended until the court's final decision on whether or not to declare the company bankrupt.
"We'll wait for the final decision of the court. In the meantime, Clabecq remains suspended," a bourse official told Reuters.
"If the court had decided to declare Clabecq bankrupt, we would immediately have delisted it," he added.

Clabecq shares closed down seven francs at 76 on the Brussels bourse on Thursday, with bid and ask prices as low as twelve francs. The cash market stock is subjected to twice daily fixings, and a maximum 10 percent markdown each day had been imposed due to the excess of sellers.

Clabecq had been struggling to survive in a heavily cyclical industry marked by overcapacity and cheap imports from eastern Europe, and had failed to find a partner to improve its competitive position.
A report on the company commissioned by the Walloon region earlier this year showed its costs were 20 to 30 percent above the average of its competitors.
